1	/**
2	 * Commerce/ProductItem — Storybook stories for the cart line-item shell (SFCC-270, plan
3	 * step 2.2), restyled to the Figma cart-item spec.
4	 *
5	 * Providers supplied by .storybook/preview.tsx: IntlProvider, ChakraProvider.
6	 * This file adds its own inert provider stack, matching product-view/index.stories.tsx's own
7	 * documented pattern (see that file for the full rationale):
8	 *   MemoryRouter — item-name.tsx's <Link> (react-router-dom) and useMultiSite (via
9	 *     MultiSiteProvider below) both need Router/site context.
10	 *   MultiSiteProvider — useMultiSite (item-name.tsx's <Link>'s buildUrl, and
11	 *     StoreLocatorProvider below, which reads the current site to namespace its localStorage key).
12	 *   StoreLocatorProvider — `useDerivedProduct` (via item-price.tsx/item-attributes.tsx's own
13	 *     transitive dependency chain) unconditionally calls `useSelectedStore()`
14	 *     (`use-selected-store.js`), which throws `'useSelectedStore must be used within a
15	 *     StoreLocatorProvider'` with no Provider present — round 2 rework fix, confirmed by reading
16	 *     that hook's source, not assumed. Nested inside MultiSiteProvider (its own body calls
17	 *     useMultiSite()), outside CommerceProviders (its one consumer, `useSelectedStore`'s internal
18	 *     `useStores` call, resolves with `enabled: false` here since no story sets a selected store
19	 *     in localStorage, so it never actually needs Commerce context — but this file nests it
20	 *     inside CommerceProviders anyway for a single consistent provider order). `config={{}}` is a
21	 *     deliberately empty stand-in — no story here drives real store-locator state, so there is no
22	 *     real config value to supply; PropTypes will warn on the missing required fields, which is
23	 *     inert noise, not a render failure.
24	 *   CommerceApiProvider + QueryClientProvider — item-attributes.tsx's usePromotions/
25	 *     useProducts/useProduct/useCurrentBasket (via
26	 *     `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-current-basket`). `disableAuthInit` +
27	 *     an `.invalid` proxy URL prevent any real network calls; none of this story's mock line
28	 *     items carry priceAdjustments/bundledProductItems/type.bundle, so every one of those
29	 *     hooks resolves with `enabled: false` and never actually fetches.
30	 *   CurrencyProvider — useCurrency (item-price.tsx, product-item/index.tsx itself).
31	 *   ServerContext.Provider (from `@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk`, not commerce-sdk-react) —
32	 *     found live in Storybook, not anticipated: item-attributes.tsx's useCurrentBasket() call
33	 *     above has its own separate transitive chain (useSFPayments -> useAppOrigin -> useOrigin)
34	 *     that calls the SDK's useServerContext() and destructures `res` from it unconditionally.
35	 *     With no Provider, useContext returns undefined and the destructure throws before useOrigin's
36	 *     own `typeof window !== 'undefined'` branch (which never touches `res` at all) is reached.
37	 *     `value={{}}` matches exactly what the real app's own browser bootstrap supplies
38	 *     client-side (`ssr/browser/main.js`'s `OuterApp`) — confirmed by reading that file.
39	 *
40	 * `GiftCard` story (round 2 rework): renders `ProductItem` with the new `hideStepperAndActions`
41	 * prop (SFCC-270 round 2, session-notes.md §11.2) set to true, on a plausible mock line item —
42	 * NOT a real gift-card detection, which this build still cannot do (see index.tsx's own docblock;
43	 * unchanged finding from the prior round). This story demonstrates the capability half only:
44	 * that when a caller explicitly asks to hide the stepper/actions, neither renders.
45	 */
46	import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-webpack5';
47	import { fn } from 'storybook/test';
48	import React from 'react';
49	import { MemoryRouter } from 'react-router-dom';
50	import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';
51	import { CommerceApiProvider } from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react';
52	import { CurrencyProvider, MultiSiteProvider, StoreLocatorProvider } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/contexts';
53	import { ServerContext } from '@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk/ssr/universal/contexts';
54	import ProductItem from '.';
55	
56	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

1	/**
2	 * SFCC-270 round 2 rework, extended post-rework (found live in Storybook by Marcel, not by this
3	 * suite). Proves three stacked bugs are actually fixed TOGETHER, not just that the symbols were
4	 * added:
5	 *   1. `useVariationAttributes` -> `isVariantValueOrderable` (base SFCC hook, unconditional
6	 *      `product.variants.filter(...)`) needs `variants` to be an array on the mock product.
7	 *   2. `useDerivedProduct` unconditionally calls `useSelectedStore()`, which throws without a
8	 *      real `StoreLocatorProvider` ancestor.
9	 *   3. `item-attributes.tsx`'s `useCurrentBasket()` call has its own separate transitive chain
10	 *      (`useSFPayments` -> `useAppOrigin` -> `useOrigin`) that calls the SDK's
11	 *      `useServerContext()` and destructures `res` from it unconditionally, before `useOrigin`'s
12	 *      own `typeof window !== 'undefined'` branch (which never touches `res`) is reached. This
13	 *      file previously mocked `useCurrentBasket` away entirely, which hid this bug completely —
14	 *      unmocked now so this suite actually exercises the real chain. `ServerContext.Provider`
15	 *      with `value={{}}` matches exactly what the real app's own browser bootstrap supplies
16	 *      client-side (`ssr/browser/main.js`'s `OuterApp`) — confirmed by reading that file.
17	 *
18	 * Deliberately does NOT use index.test.tsx's harness — that file mocks the whole
19	 * `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks` barrel's `useDerivedProduct`, which would hide both
20	 * bugs this file exists to catch. This renders through the real, unmocked `useDerivedProduct` ->
21	 * `useVariationAttributes` -> `isVariantValueOrderable` / `useSelectedStore` chain, with a real
22	 * `StoreLocatorProvider` ancestor.
23	 *
24	 * `useMultiSite` and `useCurrency` are still mocked, for a reason that has nothing to do with
25	 * this build's own logic: `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/contexts` (the barrel both
26	 * `MultiSiteProvider`/`CurrencyProvider` and `use-multi-site.js`/`use-currency.js` resolve
27	 * through) is a `.js` file containing inline JSX, which Vite's transform cannot parse as a
28	 * plain `.js` file — confirmed empirically (this file's first draft imported `MultiSiteProvider`
29	 * from that barrel directly and vitest failed at import-analysis on
30	 * `app/contexts/index.js:49`, not at any assertion). This is the same parse failure
31	 * item-variant/index.test.tsx's own docblock already documents and works around by mocking
32	 * `use-multi-site` instead of using a real `MultiSiteProvider`; extended here to `useCurrency`
33	 * for the same reason. `StoreLocatorProvider` itself is real: `use-selected-store.js` and
34	 * `store-locator-provider.jsx` both import `StoreLocatorContext` via that file's own direct path
35	 * (`.../app/contexts/store-locator-provider`), never through the barrel, so it never hits this
36	 * parse wall — confirmed by reading both files' imports, not assumed.
37	 *
38	 * Two more pragmatic mocks, both explained inline at their own `vi.mock`/`beforeEach`: `useStores`
39	 * (an unrelated dual-module-instance QueryClient issue, not this build's own code) and a
40	 * `window.matchMedia` polyfill (jsdom has none; item-price.tsx's `useBreakpointValue` needs it —
41	 * the same pre-existing gap and fix product-item/index.test.tsx's own `beforeEach` already uses).
42	 * Neither affects what this file actually proves: that a real `StoreLocatorProvider` ancestor and
43	 * an array-valued `variants` together stop the render from throwing.
44	 */
45	import React from 'react';
46	import { describe, test, expect, vi, beforeEach } from 'vitest';
47	import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
48	import { ChakraProvider } from '@chakra-ui/react';
49	import { IntlProvider } from 'react-intl';
50	import { MemoryRouter } from 'react-router-dom';
51	import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';
52	import { CommerceApiProvider } from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react';
53	import { StoreLocatorProvider } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/contexts/store-locator-provider';
54	import { ServerContext } from '@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk/ssr/universal/contexts';
55	import theme from 'app/theme';
56	import ProductItem from '.';
57	
58	vi.mock('@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-multi-site', () => ({
59	  default: vi.fn(() => ({ site: { id: 'ZimmermannAU' }, buildUrl: (path: string) => path })),
60	}));
61	
62	// Cannot use this factory's `importOriginal` here: it resolves the barrel itself
63	// (`app/hooks/index.js`), which re-exports `useCurrency` from `use-currency.js`, which imports
64	// `CurrencyContext` from the broken `app/contexts` barrel — so `importOriginal()` transitively
65	// hits the same parse wall as importing `MultiSiteProvider` does (confirmed empirically: this
66	// was the first thing tried here, and it failed at the identical `app/contexts/index.js:49`
67	// parse error). `vi.importActual` on `use-derived-product`'s own direct sub-path sidesteps it —
68	// that file's own dependency chain never touches `app/contexts` (confirmed by grepping it and
69	// every hook it imports).
70	vi.mock('@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks', async () => {
71	  const { useDerivedProduct } = await vi.importActual<
72	    typeof import('@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-derived-product')
73	  >('@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-derived-product');
74	  return {

76	    useDerivedProduct,

78	});

89	// the identical top-level-side-effect crash the mock above already works around for

91	// icon never needs to render distinguishably — testing.md's own documented canonical form

98	// same reason as product-item/index.test.tsx's own): the REAL `useSelectedStore` (unmocked, the
99	// actual thing this file proves doesn't throw) calls it internally, and the real `useStores` hit

101	// this file's own `QueryClientProvider` (a dual-module-instance style mismatch, not anything this
102	// build's own code controls). Mocking only `useStores` still exercises `useSelectedStore`'s own
103	// real body — including the `useContext(StoreLocatorContext)` throw-if-missing check this file
104	// exists to prove no longer throws — while sidestepping that unrelated plumbing issue.

112	    useStores: () => ({ data: undefined, isLoading: false }),
113	    // Same dual-module-instance QueryClient issue as useStores above, surfacing here now that
114	    // useCurrentBasket (unmocked, see this file's own docblock) calls this for real internally.
115	    useCustomerBaskets: () => ({ data: undefined, isLoading: false }),
116	  };
117	});

119	const storyQueryClient = new QueryClient({
120	  defaultOptions: { queries: { retry: false, refetchOnWindowFocus: false } },
121	});
122	
123	// `useStores` (called for real inside the real `useSelectedStore`, unmocked above) is left real
124	// too — it resolves with `enabled: false` (no selectedStoreId in this jsdom's empty
125	// localStorage), so it registers a disabled query and never actually fetches, matching
126	// index.stories.tsx's own documented reasoning for its inert CommerceApiProvider/proxy setup.
127	const renderWithStoryProviders = (ui: React.ReactElement) =>
128	  render(
129	    <ServerContext.Provider value={{}}>
130	      <ChakraProvider theme={theme}>
131	        <MemoryRouter>
132	          <QueryClientProvider client={storyQueryClient}>
133	            <CommerceApiProvider
134	              clientId="00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
135	              organizationId="f_ecom_storybook_001"
136	              shortCode="storybook"
137	              siteId="ZimmermannAU"
138	              locale="en-AU"
139	              currency="AUD"
140	              proxy="https://storybook.invalid/mobify/proxy/api"
141	              redirectURI="https://storybook.invalid/callback"
142	              disableAuthInit
143	              silenceWarnings
144	            >
145	              <StoreLocatorProvider config={{ defaultCountryCode: 'AU', defaultPostalCode: '2000' }}>
146	                <IntlProvider locale="en-AU" defaultLocale="en-AU">
147	                  {ui}
148	                </IntlProvider>
149	              </StoreLocatorProvider>
150	            </CommerceApiProvider>
151	          </QueryClientProvider>
152	        </MemoryRouter>
153	      </ChakraProvider>
154	    </ServerContext.Provider>,
155	  );
156	
157	// Mirrors index.stories.tsx's own MOCK_LINE_ITEM shape, including the round 2 `variants: []` fix.
158	const MOCK_LINE_ITEM = {
159	  itemId: 'a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6',
160	  productId: '25595021M',
161	  id: '25595021M',
162	  productName: 'Lilac Sand Silk Midi Dress',
163	  name: 'Lilac Sand Silk Midi Dress',
164	  price: 495,
165	  priceAfterItemDiscount: 495,
166	  pricePerUnit: 495,
167	  quantity: 1,
168	  stepQuantity: 1,
169	  minOrderQuantity: 1,
170	  imageGroups: [
171	    {
172	      viewType: 'small',
173	      images: [{ alt: 'Lilac Sand Silk Midi Dress', link: 'https://example.invalid/lilac-sand.jpg' }],
174	    },
175	  ],
176	  variationAttributes: [
177	    { id: 'color', name: 'Colour', values: [{ value: 'JJ5FUXX', name: 'Lilac Sand', orderable: true }] },
178	    { id: 'size', name: 'Size', values: [{ value: 'ONESIZE', name: 'One Size', orderable: true }] },
179	  ],
180	  variationValues: { color: 'JJ5FUXX', size: 'ONESIZE' },
181	  variants: [],
182	};

184	describe('ProductItem — Storybook story render (SFCC-270 round 2)', () => {
185	  // jsdom has no matchMedia implementation, and item-price.tsx's `isDesktop` uses
186	  // useBreakpointValue internally, which calls it — unrelated to either bug this file exists to
187	  // catch, same pre-existing gap and same per-file polyfill product-item/index.test.tsx's own
188	  // beforeEach already uses (not a change to the frozen vitest.setup.ts).
189	  beforeEach(() => {
190	    Object.defineProperty(window, 'matchMedia', {
191	      writable: true,
192	      value: vi.fn().mockImplementation((query: string) => ({
193	        matches: false,

195	        onchange: null,

205	  test('Default-equivalent: renders through the real, unmocked useDerivedProduct/useSelectedStore chain without throwing', () => {
206	    expect(() =>

209	      ),

212	    expect(screen.getByRole('heading', { level: 2 })).toHaveTextContent('Lilac Sand Silk Midi Dress');

10	import {useIntl} from 'react-intl'
11	import {useVariationParams} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-variation-params'
12	import {useVariationAttributes} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-variation-attributes'
13	import {useSelectedStore} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-selected-store'
14	
15	const OUT_OF_STOCK = 'OUT_OF_STOCK'
16	const UNFULFILLABLE = 'UNFULFILLABLE'
17	
18	const getInventoryById = (product, inventoryId) => {
19	    if (!inventoryId || !product?.inventories) {
20	        return null
21	    }
22	    return product.inventories.find((inv) => inv.id === inventoryId)
23	}

27	export const useDerivedProduct = (
28	    product,
29	    isProductPartOfSet = false,
30	    isProductPartOfBundle = false,
31	    pickupInStore = false,
32	    controlledVariationValues = null,
33	    onVariationChange = null
34	) => {
35	    const showLoading = !product
36	    const isProductABundle = product?.type?.bundle
37	    const stockLevel = product?.inventory?.stockLevel || 0
38	    const stepQuantity = product?.stepQuantity || 1
39	    const minOrderQuantity = stockLevel > 0 ? product?.minOrderQuantity || 1 : 0
40	    const initialQuantity = product?.quantity || product?.minOrderQuantity || 1
41	
42	    // used for product bundles when there are multiple products
43	    const lowestStockLevelProductName = product?.inventory?.lowestStockLevelProductName
44	    const intl = useIntl()
45	    const variant = useVariant(
46	        product,
47	        isProductPartOfSet,
48	        isProductPartOfBundle,
49	        controlledVariationValues
50	    )
51	    const isStandardProduct = product?.type?.item
52	    const variationParams = useVariationParams(
53	        product,
54	        isProductPartOfSet,
55	        isProductPartOfBundle,
56	        controlledVariationValues
57	    )
58	    const variationAttributes = useVariationAttributes(
59	        product,
60	        isProductPartOfSet,
61	        isProductPartOfBundle,
62	        controlledVariationValues,
63	        onVariationChange
64	    )
65	    const [quantity, setQuantity] = useState(initialQuantity)
66	    const {selectedStore} = useSelectedStore()
67	
68	    // A product is considered out of stock if the stock level is 0 or if we have all our
69	    // variation attributes selected, but don't have a variant. We do this because the API
70	    // will sometimes return all the variants even if they are out of stock, but for other
71	    // products it won't.
72	    const isOutOfStock =
73	        !stockLevel ||
74	        (!isProductABundle &&
75	            !variant &&
76	            !isStandardProduct &&
77	            Object.keys(variationParams).length === variationAttributes.length) ||
78	        (!isProductABundle && variant && !variant.orderable)
79	    const unfulfillable = stockLevel < quantity
80	
81	    // Product details for selected store
82	    const selectedStoreInventory = getInventoryById(product, selectedStore?.inventoryId)
83	    const selectedStoreStockLevel = selectedStoreInventory?.stockLevel || 0
84	    const selectedStoreLowestStockLevelProductName =
85	        selectedStoreInventory?.lowestStockLevelProductName
86	    // selectedStoreStockLevel and selectedStoreInventory are already variant specific,
87	    // so we don't need to check for variation attributes
88	    const isSelectedStoreOutOfStock = !selectedStoreStockLevel || !selectedStoreInventory?.orderable
89	    const selectedStoreUnfulfillable = selectedStoreStockLevel < quantity

132	// Chakra Components
133	import {
134	  Box,
135	  Fade,
136	  Flex,

139	  useMultiStyleConfig,
140	} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui';

142	// Project Components
143	import { HideOnDesktop, HideOnMobile } from '../responsive';
144	import ItemVariantProvider from '../item-variant';

146	import CartItemVariantName from '../item-variant/item-name';

160	const ZIMM_CART_ITEM_RECIPE = 'ZimmCartItem';
161	
162	type SfccProduct = any;
163	
164	type ProductItemProps = {
165	  product: SfccProduct;
166	  primaryAction?: React.ReactNode;
167	  secondaryActions?: React.ReactNode;
168	  deliveryActions?: React.ReactNode;
169	  onItemQuantityChange?: (quantity: number) => any;
170	  /**
171	   * Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render
172	   * body — kept here only to mirror that declared surface one-for-one (zero functional diff,
173	   * SFCC-270). No return-type guarantee to derive from PropTypes.func, so typed loosely.
174	   */
175	  onAddItemToCart?: (...args: any[]) => any;
176	  showLoading?: boolean;
177	  /** Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render body — see onAddItemToCart above. */
178	  isWishlistItem?: boolean;
179	  containerStyles?: Record<string, any>;
180	  isRemoving?: boolean;
181	  pickupInStore?: boolean;

183	   * Gift-card capability slot (SFCC-270 round 2 rework, session-notes.md §11.2): when true,

185	   * deliveryActions). Defaults falsy so every existing caller's rendering is unchanged. This
186	   * component does not itself detect a gift-card line item — see this file's own docblock — a
187	   * caller sets this explicitly once real detection exists.
188	   */
189	  hideStepperAndActions?: boolean;
190	  /**
191	   * Cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2), rendered via
192	   * ZimmInlineMessage between the quantity stepper and the actions row. Presentation only — see
193	   * ZimmInlineMessage's own docblock: this component does not itself determine OOS/partial-OOS/
194	   * unavailable/max-quantity state, a caller passes the already-resolved variant + copy.
195	   * Undefined (the default for every existing caller) renders nothing and leaves the Item
196	   * Details gap at its existing 12px desktop value.
197	   */
198	  message?: {
199	    variant: 'error' | 'warning';
200	    text: string;
201	  };
202	  /**
203	   * Discount label rendered beneath the quantity stepper (SFCC-795 §4/§11.2, plan step 3.3),
204	   * e.g. "20% off applied". Purely presentational — this component does not compute or derive a
205	   * discount percentage/label itself; a caller passes the already-resolved string once the
206	   * promotions engine is wired (not yet, this sprint — see this file's own docblock). Undefined
207	   * (every existing caller today) renders nothing — no empty node is emitted.

274	    );
275	  };

287	                  <CartItemVariantAttributes excludeBonusLabel combineAttributeValues />
288	                  <HideOnDesktop>
289	                    <Box marginTop={2}>

291	                    </Box>
292	                  </HideOnDesktop>
293	                </Stack>
294	                {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
295	                  <HideOnMobile>{deliveryActions}</HideOnMobile>
296	                )}
297	              </Flex>
298	
299	              {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
300	                <HideOnDesktop>{deliveryActions}</HideOnDesktop>
301	              )}
302	
303	              <Flex align="flex-end" justify="space-between">
304	                <Stack spacing={1}>
305	                  {!hideStepperAndActions &&
306	                    !(isRemoving && product.bonusProductLineItem) &&
307	                    (product.bonusProductLineItem ? (
308	                      <BonusProductQuantity product={product} />
309	                    ) : (
310	                      <ZimmQuantityStepper
311	                        quantity={quantity}
312	                        min={1}
313	                        max={getMaxOrderQuantity(product)}
314	                        onDecrement={handleStepperQuantityChange}
315	                        onIncrement={handleStepperQuantityChange}
316	                      />
317	                    ))}
318	                </Stack>
319	                <Stack>
320	                  <HideOnMobile>
321	                    <CartItemVariantPrice currency={activeCurrency} />
322	                  </HideOnMobile>
323	                  {!hideStepperAndActions && <HideOnMobile>{primaryAction}</HideOnMobile>}
324	                </Stack>
325	              </Flex>
326	
327	              {/* SFCC-795 (plan step 3.3): discount label, directly beneath the stepper/price row

332	              )}

334	              {/* SFCC-795 §11.2: sits between the stepper (above) and the actions row (the
335	                  existing inventory Box below, secondaryActions, and the mobile primaryAction
336	                  block further down) — prop-driven only, see this file's own docblock. */}
337	              {message && <ZimmInlineMessage variant={message.variant} text={message.text} />}
338	
339	              <Box>
340	                {product && showInventoryMessage && (
341	                  <Fade in={true}>
342	                    <Text color="orange.600" fontWeight={600}>
343	                      {inventoryMessage}
344	                    </Text>
345	                  </Fade>
346	                )}
347	              </Box>
348	
349	              {!hideStepperAndActions && secondaryActions}
350	            </Stack>
351	          </Flex>
352	
353	          {!hideStepperAndActions && (
354	            <HideOnDesktop>
355	              <Box w={'full'}>{primaryAction}</Box>
356	            </HideOnDesktop>
357	          )}
358	        </Stack>
359	      </ItemVariantProvider>
360	    </Box>
361	  );
362	};
363	
364	export default ProductItem;

import LoadingSpinner from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/loading-spinner';
import BonusProductQuantity from './bonus-product-quantity';
import { ZimmInlineMessage } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmInlineMessage';
import { ZimmQuantityStepper } from 'app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmQuantityStepper';

// Hooks
import { useCurrency, useDerivedProduct } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks';

// Utils
import { getMaxOrderQuantity } from 'app/utils/maxOrderQuantity';

const ZIMM_CART_ITEM_RECIPE = 'ZimmCartItem';

type SfccProduct = any;

type ProductItemProps = {
  product: SfccProduct;
  primaryAction?: React.ReactNode;
  secondaryActions?: React.ReactNode;
  deliveryActions?: React.ReactNode;
  onItemQuantityChange?: (quantity: number) => any;
  /**
   * Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render
   * body — kept here only to mirror that declared surface one-for-one (zero functional diff,
   * SFCC-270). No return-type guarantee to derive from PropTypes.func, so typed loosely.
   */
  onAddItemToCart?: (...args: any[]) => any;
  showLoading?: boolean;
  /** Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render body — see onAddItemToCart above. */
  isWishlistItem?: boolean;
  containerStyles?: Record<string, any>;
  isRemoving?: boolean;
  pickupInStore?: boolean;
  /**
   * Gift-card capability slot (SFCC-270 round 2 rework, session-notes.md §11.2): when true,
   * suppresses the quantity stepper and every actions surface (primaryAction, secondaryActions,
   * deliveryActions). Defaults falsy so every existing caller's rendering is unchanged. This
   * component does not itself detect a gift-card line item — see this file's own docblock — a
   * caller sets this explicitly once real detection exists.
   */
  hideStepperAndActions?: boolean;
  /**
   * Cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2), rendered via
   * ZimmInlineMessage between the quantity stepper and the actions row. Presentation only — see
   * ZimmInlineMessage's own docblock: this component does not itself determine OOS/partial-OOS/
   * unavailable/max-quantity state, a caller passes the already-resolved variant + copy.
   * Undefined (the default for every existing caller) renders nothing and leaves the Item
   * Details gap at its existing 12px desktop value.
   */
  message?: {
    variant: 'error' | 'warning';
    text: string;
  };
  /**
   * Discount label rendered beneath the quantity stepper (SFCC-795 §4/§11.2, plan step 3.3),
   * e.g. "20% off applied". Purely presentational — this component does not compute or derive a
   * discount percentage/label itself; a caller passes the already-resolved string once the
   * promotions engine is wired (not yet, this sprint — see this file's own docblock). Undefined
   * (every existing caller today) renders nothing — no empty node is emitted.
   *
   * Styling: rendered via `ZimmInlineMessage variant="success"`, not a bespoke element —
   * corrected 2026-09-18 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull for this exact node, superseding
   * the prior, wrong precedent this JSDoc used to cite). The pulled node is `color:
   * var(--alias-color-text-success, #2D5A3D); font-size: var(--brand-font-size-300, 12px);
   * font-weight: 400; line-height: var(--brand-font-lineHeight-450, 18px)` — "Default/Caption",
   * byte-identical to this codebase's own `status.success` token (green[500] = '#2d5a3d',
   * theme/foundation/colour.ts:27,80, registered as var(--zimm-color-status-success) in
   * zimmTokens.ts:73) and the exact same node family `ZimmInlineMessage`'s `error`/`warning`
   * variants already render (regular weight, 12px/18px — see that component's own docblock). The
   * previous version of this comment cited item-variant.css.ts's `colourSize` part as "the
   * nearest existing sibling treatment" and stated no Figma node existed for this element — both
   * wrong: `colourSize` is a DIFFERENT, MEDIUM-weight node ("Default/Caption-strong", the "Lilac
   * Sand, One size" line), and a real node did exist, just not yet pulled. Confirmed directly
   * with Marcel: no icon on this variant (matching `error`'s own no-icon behaviour, unlike
   * `warning`).
   */
  discountLabel?: string;
};

/**
 * Component representing a product item usually in a list with details about the product - name, variant, pricing, etc.
 * @param {Object} product Product to be represented in the list item.
 * @param {node} primaryAction Child component representing the most prominent action to be performed by the user.
 * @param {node} secondaryActions Child component representing the other actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
 * @param {node} deliveryActions Child component representing the delivery actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
 * @param {func} onItemQuantityChange callback function to be invoked whenever item quantity changes.
 * @param {boolean} showLoading Renders a loading spinner with overlay if set to true.
 * @returns A JSX element representing product item in a list (eg: wishlist, cart, etc).
 */
const ProductItem = ({
  product,
  primaryAction,
  secondaryActions,
  deliveryActions,
  // CodeRabbit (SFCC-11 cumulative review): default was `noop`, a synchronous no-op returning
  // `undefined` - but product-quantity-picker.tsx's handleQuantityChange unconditionally calls
  // `.then(...)` on this callback's return value. A caller that omits this optional prop and
  // then changes quantity would throw. This default resolves to `true` (a valid change) so the
  // `.then` chain completes normally instead.
  onItemQuantityChange = async () => true,
  showLoading = false,
  containerStyles = {},
  isRemoving = false,
  pickupInStore = false,
  hideStepperAndActions = false,
  message,
  discountLabel,
}: ProductItemProps) => {
  const { showInventoryMessage, inventoryMessage, quantity, setQuantity } = useDerivedProduct(
    product,
    false,
    false,
    pickupInStore,
  );
  const { currency: activeCurrency } = useCurrency();
  // hasError drives ZimmCartItem's own Item Details gap widening (12px -> 16px desktop) — see
  // product-item.css.ts's docblock — derived from `message`, not a separate prop, so the two can
  // never disagree about whether an error-variant message is currently showing.
  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_CART_ITEM_RECIPE, { hasError: message?.variant === 'error' });
  // SFCC-271-250 (plan step 3.5): shared by both ZimmQuantityStepper callbacks below — see this
  // file's own docblock for why this exact call order (real mutation first, conditional local
  // commit second) is load-bearing, not incidental.
  const handleStepperQuantityChange = (nextQuantity: number) => {
    void Promise.resolve(onItemQuantityChange(nextQuantity)).then(
      (isValidChange: boolean) => isValidChange && setQuantity(nextQuantity),
    );
  };
  return (
    <Box position="relative" data-testid={`sf-cart-item-${product.productId ? product.productId : product.id}`}>
      <ItemVariantProvider variant={product}>
        {showLoading && <LoadingSpinner />}
        <Stack layerStyle="cardBordered" align="flex-start" {...containerStyles}>
          <Flex sx={styles.row} width="full" backgroundColor="white">
            <CartItemVariantImage />
            <Stack sx={styles.details} flex={1}>
              <Flex sx={styles.info}>
                <Stack spacing={1}>
                  <CartItemVariantName />
                  <CartItemVariantAttributes excludeBonusLabel combineAttributeValues />
                  <HideOnDesktop>
                    <Box marginTop={2}>
                      <CartItemVariantPrice align="left" currency={activeCurrency} />
                    </Box>
                  </HideOnDesktop>
                </Stack>
                {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
                  <HideOnMobile>{deliveryActions}</HideOnMobile>
                )}
              </Flex>

              {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
                <HideOnDesktop>{deliveryActions}</HideOnDesktop>
              )}

              <Flex align="flex-end" justify="space-between">
                <Stack spacing={1}>
                  {!hideStepperAndActions &&
                    !(isRemoving && product.bonusProductLineItem) &&
                    (product.bonusProductLineItem ? (
                      <BonusProductQuantity product={product} />
                    ) : (
                      <ZimmQuantityStepper
                        quantity={quantity}
                        min={1}
                        max={getMaxOrderQuantity(product)}
                        onDecrement={handleStepperQuantityChange}
                        onIncrement={handleStepperQuantityChange}
                      />
                    ))}
                </Stack>
                <Stack>
                  <HideOnMobile>
                    <CartItemVariantPrice currency={activeCurrency} />
                  </HideOnMobile>
                  {!hideStepperAndActions && <HideOnMobile>{primaryAction}</HideOnMobile>}
                </Stack>
              </Flex>

              {/* SFCC-795 (plan step 3.3): discount label, directly beneath the stepper/price row
                  above, ahead of the inline message below — prop-driven only, no empty node when
                  omitted. See the `discountLabel` prop's own JSDoc for the styling citation. */}
              {discountLabel && (
                <ZimmInlineMessage variant="success" text={discountLabel} dataTestId="zimm-discount-label" />
              )}

              {/* SFCC-795 §11.2: sits between the stepper (above) and the actions row (the
                  existing inventory Box below, secondaryActions, and the mobile primaryAction
                  block further down) — prop-driven only, see this file's own docblock. */}
              {message && <ZimmInlineMessage variant={message.variant} text={message.text} />}

              <Box>
                {product && showInventoryMessage && (
                  <Fade in={true}>
                    <Text color="orange.600" fontWeight={600}>
                      {inventoryMessage}
                    </Text>
                  </Fade>
                )}
              </Box>

              {!hideStepperAndActions && secondaryActions}
            </Stack>
          </Flex>

          {!hideStepperAndActions && (
            <HideOnDesktop>
              <Box w={'full'}>{primaryAction}</Box>
            </HideOnDesktop>
          )}
        </Stack>
      </ItemVariantProvider>
    </Box>
  );
};

export default ProductItem;

Step 3.5 done on `feature/SFCC-11_cart` (confirmed not on develop/main before starting). Two files touched, both explicitly named in the step's own pass-criteria text:

- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/product-item/index.tsx`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/product-item/index.test.tsx`

Nothing else in the working tree changed (`git status --porcelain` shows exactly these two, no untracked files). Not staged, not committed.

## What actually changed, and why it matters

The cart's quantity buttons used to be plain, unstyled base-SFCC controls with no upper limit at all — a shopper could click "+" forever. Now they're the real Zimmermann stepper, and clicking "+" past the product's cap (3 by default, or whatever the site preference says once that backend hook ships) visibly stops working instead of silently accepting bad quantities. Nothing about *how* the cart actually saves a quantity change to the server changed — that logic was copied over exactly, not rewritten.

**`product-item/index.tsx`** — in the one render branch that isn't the bonus/free-gift line (`BonusProductQuantity`'s branch is byte-for-byte untouched — see the diff below, no `+`/`-` marks on that line at all), swapped `ProductQuantityPicker` for `ZimmQuantityStepper`, and wired `getMaxOrderQuantity(product)` as `max` and `min={1}`. Removed the now-unused `ProductQuantityPicker` import and the now-unused `stepQuantity` destructure (it was only ever passed to the picker I just removed).

## The part you told me to scrutinize hardest: the mutation wrapper

The risk was: point the stepper's buttons straight at the local `setQuantity` (tempting, matches the stepper's own Storybook demo), and the number on screen would update while the real basket on the server silently stops changing.

I didn't do that. I added one function, shared by both buttons:

```ts
const handleStepperQuantityChange = (nextQuantity: number) => {
  void Promise.resolve(onItemQuantityChange(nextQuantity)).then(
    (isValidChange: boolean) => isValidChange && setQuantity(nextQuantity),
  );
};
```

This is the exact same two-step contract as the old `handleQuantityChange` (`product-quantity-picker.tsx`, untouched) — call the real mutation first, only write to local state if that call comes back truthy. The only thing that changed is the input shape: the old picker parsed a raw `<input>` change event; `ZimmQuantityStepper` hands `onDecrement`/`onIncrement` the already-computed next number directly, so there's no parsing step left to do, but the "real call, then conditional commit" order is identical. Passed as `onDecrement={handleStepperQuantityChange}` and `onIncrement={handleStepperQuantityChange}` — one function satisfies both, since both need the same next-value handed straight through.
